title: KPT step 2: common single consonants
summary: Learn three common weak changes without mixing in double consonants or clusters.

sections.title: Three changes only
paragraphs: A single consonant can change rather than merely shorten. In this block, k disappears, p becomes v, or t becomes d.
Both complete forms are supplied during recognition.

sections.title: Compare the same position
paragraphs: Find the consonant in the first form and compare the same part of the second form.
The symbol ∅ means that no letter remains in that position.

examples.english: foot or leg → of the foot or leg
steps: The k is absent in the weak form: k → ∅.
The other letters remain visible around that position.
The p becomes v: p → v.
The final -n belongs to the complete noun form.
The t becomes d: t → d.
Keep the Finnish vowels ö and ä unchanged.

commonMistakes: Do not remove every k in Finnish.
Do not change p to b; the taught change is p → v.
Do not replace Finnish d with English-style spelling.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in jalka (“foot or leg”) → jalan (“of the foot or leg”)?
practiceExercises.explanation: The single k disappears in the supplied weak form.

optionFeedback.k → ∅: Correct. The single k disappears in the supplied weak form.
optionFeedback.k → j: “k → j” does not show the required pattern. The single k disappears in the supplied weak form.
optionFeedback.kk → k: “kk → k” does not show the required pattern. The single k disappears in the supplied weak form.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in leipä (“bread”) → leivän (“of the bread”)?

optionFeedback.p → v: Correct. The single p becomes v.
optionFeedback.pp → p: “pp → p” does not show the required pattern. The single p becomes v.
optionFeedback.t → d: “t → d” does not show the required pattern. The single p becomes v.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in pöytä (“table”) → pöydän (“of the table”)?

optionFeedback.t → d: Correct. The single t becomes d.
optionFeedback.tt → t: “tt → t” does not show the required pattern. The single t becomes d.
optionFeedback.lt → ll: “lt → ll” does not show the required pattern. The single t becomes d.

practiceExercises.prompt: hakea (“to fetch”), supplied stem hake- + minä -n → ____ (“I fetch”) · k disappears
practiceExercises.explanation: The supplied target means “I fetch”. Use the supplied stem hake- and minä ending -n, let k disappear, and combine the parts: hakea → haen.
